Original asks: DLC for strategy video game released over 3 years after release. Master's thesis on postcolonialism in this game for American University in 2023 advised by academic who completed two degrees at California University and published 2020 monograph on video games. DLC made changes to mechanics including religion and technology, new mechanics for specific playable European nation. What full name of third content designer credited for this DLC?

Skeleton:
R1 DLC and game release interval: need DLC released for strategy video game over three years after its release.
R2 Game and postcolonialism thesis: Master's thesis written on theme postcolonialism in this game for American University in 2023.
R3 Thesis advisor and credentials: advised by academic who completed two degrees at California University and published 2020 monograph on subject of video games.
R4 DLC mechanics: DLC made changes to base game mechanics including religion and technology, and new mechanics for a specific playable European nation.
R5 Requested third designer: full name of third content designer credited for this DLC.

Claims:
C1: 2023 master's thesis '"Is EU4 Only About Map Painting?": Settler Colonial Ideology in Europa Universalis IV' by Mitchell Losito at Georgetown University.
C2: Amanda D. Phillips was advisor for 2023 Georgetown University master's thesis on Europa Universalis IV.

Need determine support. Claims identify game Europa Universalis IV? C1 says thesis on EU4, at Georgetown. Does it establish postcolonialism? Title "Settler Colonial Ideology" maybe related to colonial ideology, but not exactly postcolonialism? Need material. The requirement R2: Master's thesis written on theme of postcolonialism in this game for an American University in 2023. C1 says thesis "Settler Colonial Ideology in Europa Universalis IV", Georgetown University, 2023. Georgetown is American University? "American University" could mean a university in America, not American University specifically? Original says "for an American University" likely in U.S. Georgetown University is American. C1 says master's thesis at Georgetown. "Settler Colonial Ideology" is related to colonialism, not necessarily postcolonialism. Is that enough? Need be strict. It establishes thesis in 2023 at American University on Europa Universalis IV with settler colonial ideology. Postcolonialism? "Settler Colonial Ideology" might not equal postcolonialism, though related. The skeleton says theme of postcolonialism. C1 doesn't state postcolonialism. It states settler colonial ideology. Could be substantive part? Maybe game and thesis and year and American university. But not postcolonialism. So R2 partially supported: establishes thesis about EU4 at Georgetown 2023, but not postcolonialism theme. Also "this game" from previous requirement? R2 requires "in this game" maybe links to R1 game. Claims identify EU4. But R1 game release interval not supported. In evaluating R2 alone, it establishes thesis on EU4, so yes game. But need postcolonialism unsupported. status partially_supported.

R3: advisor academic who completed two degrees at California University and published 2020 monograph on video games. C2 says Amanda D. Phillips was advisor for thesis. It does not mention completed two degrees at California University or published 2020 monograph on video games. So unsupported? It establishes advisor identity but not credentials. Requirement material content: "advised by an academic who completed two degrees at a California University and published a 2020 monograph on the subject of video games." C2 establishes that thesis was advised by Amanda D. Phillips, so part "advised by an academic" yes, but the specific academic must have those credentials. Are those material parts? The requirement is about advisor and credentials. It establishes an advisor exists. Does that count as substantive material part? The requirement's core is advisor credentials. If it says "that was advised by an academic who completed..." The claim establishes "advised by Amanda D. Phillips", but not that she completed two degrees at California University or published 2020 monograph. So partially_supported? Need decide. For partially_supported: establish at least one substantive material part, but one or more material parts remain unsupported. Is identifying advisor a substantive part? It is an entity/role. But requirement's material conditions include advisor plus credentials. The fact she was advisor is part. C2 directly supports that the thesis was advised by Amanda D. Phillips (an academic). It doesn't support the credentials. Thus partially_supported, supported_by C2. Alternatively unsupported because requirement specifically "academic who completed two degrees..." and C2 only says advisor, not credentials; the "advised by academic" is trivial? But it's a material part. The definitions: "partially_supported: The Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported." Advisor identity is substantive. So partially_supported.

R4: DLC mechanics including religion and technology, new mechanics for specific playable European nation. Claims do not mention DLC mechanics. Unsupported. supported_by [].

R5: full name of third content designer credited for DLC. No claim. Unsupported. [].

R1: DLC release interval. Claims mention EU4 thesis but not DLC release over three years after game release. Unsupported. [].

Need be careful: C1 might establish "game" is Europa Universalis IV and maybe strategy video game? Does claim "Europa Universalis IV" imply strategy? Not without outside knowledge. It says thesis title. Could support R2 game? It names game. But R1 requires DLC and interval. No.

Could C1/C2 support R2 fully? It states thesis on "Settler Colonial Ideology", not "postcolonialism". Original "theme of postcolonialism" might be satisfied by "Settler Colonial Ideology"? Need not use outside knowledge. "Settler Colonial Ideology" is not exactly "postcolonialism"; but it is colonial ideology. It might be a theme related to colonialism. Does "postcolonialism" vs "settler colonial ideology" are distinct academic concepts. We cannot infer. So partially.

R3: C2 supports advisor Amanda D. Phillips. Maybe C1 says thesis at Georgetown, C2 says advisor. But no credentials. So partial. Need include C2 only. If R3 includes "advised by an academic" C2 supports. Good.

R2: Need consider "for an American University in 2023". C1 says Georgetown University. Is Georgetown an American University? Without outside knowledge? Could infer from name? Georgetown University could be in America? Not necessarily? The claim says "at Georgetown University", no country. But "American University" could be proper noun "American University" in Washington, D.C. Original: "for an American University in 2023" ambiguous. It might mean a university in America, not "American University" as institution. The Task Skeleton: "for an American University" capital A? It says "American University" maybe proper. C1 says Georgetown University. If it means literally American University, C1 not support. But likely original means American University as any U.S. university. However we must not use outside knowledge. Claim doesn't state American. But "Georgetown University" name? Not enough to know country. Also if "American University" proper, not match. So R2 partial for thesis, game, 2023, but not postcolonialism and maybe not American University? Actually C1 says Georgetown University. Without outside knowledge, cannot establish American University (whether proper or adjective). But the claim includes "Georgetown University" maybe an American University by name? We cannot use outside knowledge. The phrase "Georgetown University" doesn't include American. But is "Georgetown University" an American University? This is common knowledge? Not allowed outside. So maybe not fully. But partial anyway.

R2 status partial due missing postcolonialism at least. Supported_by C1. C1 also supports 2023, master's thesis, game. C2? C2 mentions advisor for the thesis on EU4. It doesn't add R2 except link? Maybe C1 alone enough for partial. C2 not needed. Could include C1 for thesis. R3 C2.
